selected_candidates.statement: An irreducible symmetric SPD M-matrix A is exactly reconstructed from n(n+1)/2 labeled scalar port responses to baseline, single shunts t/2t and pair shunts t, t>0. The inverse-M inequalities uniquely select the pair root. For K+sC with unknown positive internal shunt gains h_i, independently known diagonal C and two distinct positive real Laplace points identify all gains and K using n(n+1) scalar responses. Unknown C preserves the congruence ambiguity.

contract.assumptions: Exact real identifiability/count optimality does not imply robust physical recovery. Positive diagonal shunts cannot remove the hidden-loss depth barrier under the specified readout model. The stronger transient all-signed-input bound charges squared input, not physical work. Unequal-variance extension compares Gaussian KL, not Blackwell order. All8 noisy direct calibrations rejected or left the physical class; ordinary constrained joint fitting was stronger but small port error did not identify internal parameters. No acquired measurement, fabricated device, historical priority, efficient algorithm or practical advantage is inferred from these mathematical/model results. Mission NOT_ACHIEVED.
contract.costs: Pay interventions, calibration, settling, finite pulse tail and reset cycles. Tail bias <=Q exp(-sT)/(s C_0 U(s)), variance sigma²(1-exp(-2sT))/(2s U(s)²); longer horizon leaves nonzero noise variance. Inverse conditioning/depth can amplify tiny errors. Full waveforms may be more informative than two summaries.
